--- title: "Converting to `shinyreact`" subtitle: "Converting a Shiny app-package to a React client" author: "Martin Frigaard" date: "2026-11-15" categories: [Shiny, React, Packages] image: "image.png" draft: false toc: true toc-depth: 3 toc-title: 'Contents' toc-location: right --- I got pretty excited when I saw Posit's [blog post](https://opensource.posit.co/blog/2026-09-30_introducing-shinyreact/) announcing the `shinyreact` package. I've worked on a few [Next.js](https://nextjs.org/) apps, but couldn't really wrap my head around how a Shiny and [React](https://react.dev/) R package would work. I recently built a Shiny app-package for browsing [#TidyTuesday](https://github.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday) datasets: `ttdviewer`. I designed the UI so I could pick a dataset title and view its files in List, Summary, and Graphs tabs (the graphs come from [`inspectdf`](https://alastairrushworth.com/inspectdf/)). I can also download one file or all of a dataset's files as CSV or `parquet`. You can view the documentation and code for `ttdviewer` on its [site](https://mjfrigaard.github.io/ttdviewer/). `ttdviewer` uses `bslib` (`page_sidebar()`, `sidebar()`, and `navset_tab()`). In this post I'll cover converting the UI to [`shinyreact`](https://posit-dev.github.io/shinyreact/). I'll also cover the parts the documentation doesn't, and the few surprises I hit along the way. ## What is `shinyreact`? `shinyreact` moves the UI *out* of R. The server still holds the reactive graph (`input`, `reactive()`, `req()`, and `bindEvent()` all behave as usual), but the page is a React client we write ourselves. The diagrams below give a broad overview of how React works (left) and how `shinyreact` supplies the plumbing between the React UI and the reactive server (right): ::: {layout-ncol="2"} ```{mermaid} %%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'themeVariables': { 'fontFamily': 'monospace', 'darkMode':false}}}%% flowchart TD subgraph React["React"] direction TB Event(["User event:
click or typing"]) Set("State setter called
(useState())") Rerun("React re-runs the
component functions") JSX("New UI description
from JSX") Diff{"What
changed?"} Page("Only those changes
applied to the page") Event -->|"i. handler
updates state"| Set Set -->|"ii. schedules
a re-render"| Rerun Rerun -->|"iii. components
return markup"| JSX JSX -->|"iv. compared with
the previous output"| Diff Diff -->|"v. updates
the DOM"| Page Page -.->|"next event"| Event end style React fill:#FFFFFF,color:#000000,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px,rx:10,ry:10 style Event fill:#FFFFFF,color:#000000,stroke:#333 style Set fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF,rx:5,ry:5 style Rerun fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF,rx:5,ry:5 style JSX fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF,rx:5,ry:5 style Diff fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF style Page fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF,rx:5,ry:5 ``` ```{mermaid} %%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'themeVariables': { 'fontFamily': 'monospace', 'darkMode':false}}}%% flowchart TD subgraph SR["shinyreact"] direction TB User(["User"]) UI("Browser: React components
(ui.js, written in TSX)") JS[["Browser: shinyreact.js
hooks and React"]] RG("R server: reactive graph
input, reactive(), outputs") User -->|"i. clicks and selects"| UI UI <-->|"ii. hooks"| JS JS <-->|"iii. Shiny websocket"| RG end style SR fill:#FFFFFF,color:#000000,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px,rx:10,ry:10 style User fill:#FFFFFF,color:#000000,stroke:#333 style UI fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF,rx:5,ry:5 style JS fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF style RG fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF,rx:5,ry:5 ``` ::: `shinyreact` is pretty new (version 0.1.0), and the documentation calls it a pre-release, so it's not on CRAN: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="false"} pak::pak("posit-dev/shinyreact/pkg-r") ``` ::: The R side is small. The package exports seven functions, and `ttdviewer` only uses two of them (`page_react()` and `reactive_output()`): ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="false"} ls("package:shinyreact") #> [1] "page_bare" "page_react" "page_react_dep" "page_react_html" #> [5] "reactive_output" "send_message" "wire_tap" ``` ::: 1. `page_react()` replaces the UI function and serves a `ui.js` (and `ui.css`) from `src_dir`. The server sends no body HTML, so the client creates its own mount point. The other `page_*` functions cover setups `page_react()` doesn't: * `page_react_html()`: serves a complete `index.html` (the kind a Vite build writes) and injects the Shiny dependencies into it. * `page_react_dep()`: builds the `htmltools::htmlDependency()` for a bundle. `page_react()` calls it for us. * `page_bare()`: a bare page with jQuery and Shiny (and no Bootstrap unless we pass a `theme`). 2. `reactive_output()` sends any R value to the client as JSON. The client reads it with `useShinyOutputValue()`. 3. `send_message()` pushes a custom message from the server to a React component, which receives it with `useShinyMessageHandler()`. The message id is namespaced like an input or output id, so it works inside modules. 4. `wire_tap()` is for testing. It reads the JSON that crossed the Shiny websocket during a `shinytest2` run, so tests can check what the server actually sent to the client. ### Client hooks On the client, the hooks on `window.shinyreact` read and write Shiny values: `useShinyInput()` sets `input[[id]]`, `useShinyOutputValue()` reads a `reactive_output()`, and `ShinyOutput` and `ImageOutput` host classic Shiny outputs inside React. `ShinyModuleProvider` namespaces the hook ids, so Shiny modules still work. The diagram below shows how values move between the two sides: ```{mermaid} %%| fig-width: 6 %%| fig-align: 'center' %%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'themeVariables': { 'fontFamily': 'monospace', 'darkMode':false}}}%% flowchart LR subgraph Srv["R server"] RO[["reactive_output()"]] RX[["renderPlot()
renderUI()
downloadHandler()"]] end subgraph Cli["React client"] OV("useShinyOutputValue()") SO("ShinyOutput
ImageOutput") SI("useShinyInput()") end subgraph Inp["R server (inputs)"] IN[/"input$ds_title"/] end RO -->|"i. JSON value"| OV RX -->|"ii. classic output"| SO SI -->|"iii. user choice"| IN style Srv fill:#FFFFFF,color:#000000,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px,rx:10,ry:10 style Cli fill:#FFFFFF,color:#000000,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px,rx:10,ry:10 style Inp fill:#FFFFFF,color:#000000,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px,rx:10,ry:10 style RO fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF style RX fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF style IN fill:#FFFFFF,color:#000000,stroke:#333 style OV fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF,rx:5,ry:5 style SO fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF,rx:5,ry:5 style SI fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF,rx:5,ry:5 ``` ## Spike first Before touching the package, I asked Claude to build a spike (a small prototype). The spike tested each output with the Netflix Titles data (one file) and the Space Launches data (two files). ### The prompt The `shinyreact` documentation only shows R examples for `plotly` and `reactable`. `ttdviewer` also uses `listviewerlite`, `renderPlot()`, and `downloadHandler()`, and the client has to be served from an installed package. The prompt asked the spike to test those gaps and nothing else: ```{.default} Before we convert ttdviewer to shinyreact, build a throwaway spike outside the repo. Use shinyreact 0.1.0 from GitHub and the no build pattern (page_react() serving www/ui.js). Load ttdviewer with load_all() and test the outputs the shinyreact docs don't cover: 1. listviewerlite::listview() through renderUI() 2. inspect_plot() through renderPlot() 3. downloadHandler() for CSV and zip downloads 4. reactable (documented, but confirm it works with our data) Use Netflix Titles (one file) and Space Launches (two files). Then check that page_react() can serve the client from an installed package (inst/www/). Report what works, what breaks, and why. ``` ### The structure The spike is just two files. There's no build step: `page_react()` finds `www/ui.js`, and the client uses `React.createElement()` (aliased as `h()`) instead of JSX. ::: {style="font-style: italic;"} ```{.default} spike ├── app.R └── www └── ui.js 2 directories, 2 files ``` ::: `app.R` loads `ttdviewer` with `load_all()` and defines one output for each question in the prompt: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="true" code-summary="show/hide app.R"} library(shiny) library(shinyreact) pkgload::load_all("~/projects/apps/R/ttdviewer", quiet = TRUE) ui <- page_react(theme = bslib::bs_theme(version = 5)) server <- function(input, output, session) { data <- reactive({ req(input$title) load_tt_data(input$title) }) # i. plain values for the client output$titles <- reactive_output(sort(unique(all_tt_combined$title))) output$files <- reactive_output({ if (is.null(input$title)) return(NULL) d <- data() list(names = names(d), date = format(attr(d[[1]], "date"))) }) # ii. listviewerlite (HTML) output$list <- renderUI({ req(data()) listviewerlite::listview(data()) }) # iii. reactable (htmlwidget) output$table <- reactable::renderReactable({ req(data()) reactable::reactable(utils::head(data()[[1]], 1000), searchable = TRUE) }) # iv. inspect_plot() ggplot output$plt_types <- renderPlot({ req(data()) inspect_plot(data()[1], plots = "types") }) # v. download output$download <- downloadHandler( filename = function() tt_download_filename(data(), input$format, input$title), content = function(file) write_tt_download(data(), input$format, file) ) } shinyApp(ui, server) ``` ::: `ui.js` reads the plain values with `useShinyOutputValue()`, sends the title and format back with `useShinyInput()`, and hosts the classic outputs in `ShinyOutput` and `ImageOutput`: ```{.default} const { React, ReactDOM, useShinyInput, useShinyOutputValue, ShinyOutput, ImageOutput, } = window.shinyreact; #<1> const h = React.createElement; #<2> function App() { const titles = useShinyOutputValue("titles", []); #<3> const files = useShinyOutputValue("files", null); #<3> const [title, setTitle] = useShinyInput("title", "Netflix Titles"); #<4> const [format, setFormat] = useShinyInput("format", "csv"); #<4> return h("div", { className: "container py-3" }, h("select", { id: "title", className: "form-select mb-2", value: title, onChange: (e) => setTitle(e.target.value) }, #<5> titles.map((t) => h("option", { key: t, value: t }, t))), files && h("p", { id: "files" }, "Files: ", files.names.join(", "), " | TidyTuesday date: ", files.date), #<6> h("select", { className: "form-select mb-2", value: format, onChange: (e) => setFormat(e.target.value) }, ["csv", "parquet", "original"].map((f) => h("option", { key: f, value: f }, f))), h(ShinyOutput, { id: "download", tagName: "a", className: "btn btn-primary shiny-download-link", #<7> href: "", target: "_blank", download: "" }, "Download"), #<7> h("h4", { className: "mt-3" }, "List"), h(ShinyOutput, { id: "list", className: "shiny-html-output" }), #<8> h("h4", null, "Table"), h(ShinyOutput, { id: "table", className: "reactable html-widget html-widget-output", #<9> "data-reactable-output": "table" }), #<9> h("h4", null, "Plot"), h(ImageOutput, { id: "plt_types", width: "100%", height: "300px" }), #<10> ); } ReactDOM.createRoot(document.body.appendChild(document.createElement("div"))).render(h(App)); #<11> ``` 1. No build step means no imports: React, ReactDOM, the hooks, and the output components all come from `window.shinyreact` 2. `h()` is a short name for `React.createElement()`, which stands in for JSX 3. Plain values from `reactive_output()`: `output$titles` and `output$files` 4. Inputs sent to the server as `input$title` and `input$format` 5. Picking a title calls `setTitle()`, which updates `input$title` 6. The line that crashed on datasets with one file (see [Surprises](#surprises-in-the-spike)) 7. The download link for `downloadHandler()` 8. The `listviewerlite` HTML from `renderUI()` 9. The `reactable` widget from `renderReactable()` 10. The `inspect_plot()` image from `renderPlot()` 11. `page_react()` sends no body HTML, so the client adds its own `
` and renders `App` into it ### The outputs Every output worked once the client was fixed (see [Surprises](#surprises-in-the-spike) below). The rest of this section covers how each one is hosted on the client. #### Lists `listviewerlite::listview()` returns HTML, so the server keeps `renderUI()`, and the client hosts it with the `shiny-html-output` class (which tells Shiny to treat the element like a `uiOutput()`): ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="false"} output$list <- renderUI({ req(data()) listviewerlite::listview(data()) }) ``` ::: ```{.default} h(ShinyOutput, { id: "list", className: "shiny-html-output" }), ``` #### Tables `reactable` works the documented way: a `ShinyOutput` with the widget classes (`reactable html-widget html-widget-output`). #### Plots `ImageOutput` is only documented for Python, but it follows the same contract as R's `renderPlot()`. The client reports its size through `.clientdata_output__width` and `_height`, and draws the image `renderPlot()` sends back. The `inspect_plot()` ggplots rendered unchanged: ```{.default} h(ImageOutput, { id: "plt_types", width: "100%", height: "300px" }), ``` #### Downloads `downloadHandler()` binds to an anchor with the `shiny-download-link` class, so a `ShinyOutput` with `tagName="a"` works: ```{.default} h(ShinyOutput, { id: "download", tagName: "a", className: "btn btn-primary shiny-download-link", href: "", target: "_blank", download: "" }, "Download"), #<1> ``` 1. Shiny fills in `href` with the download URL; `target` and `download` match the attributes `downloadButton()` sets The CSV download for Netflix Titles returned 3.0 MB, and the two file zip for Space Launches returned 104 KB. #### Packaging `page_react()` passes `src_dir` to `page_react_dep()`, which builds an `htmltools::htmlDependency()` with a file source. I wanted to know whether a file source works from an installed package. I confirmed it by installing a copy of `ttdviewer` (with `ui.js` in `inst/www/`) into a temporary library: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="false"} app_ui <- function() { shinyreact::page_react( useBusyIndicators(spinners = TRUE, pulse = TRUE), src_dir = system.file("www", package = "ttdviewer"), theme = bslib::bs_theme(version = 5), title = "#TidyTuesday Viewer" ) } ``` ::: * `system.file("www", package = "ttdviewer")` found `ui.js`, and `page_react_dep()` built a `type="module"` script from it. So the built client belongs in `inst/www/`. * `bs_theme(version = 5)` keeps Bootstrap on the page, so the React components can use the same classes (`form-select`, `nav-tabs`, `card`) the `bslib` UI used. ### Surprises {#surprises-in-the-spike} The spike turned up two small surprises and one crash. `ImageOutput` worked with R's `renderPlot()` (see Plots above). And `reactable` didn't need a `reactableOutput()` placeholder, because `shinyreact` finds the widget's JavaScript from the render function. The crash came from a plain value. #### Length one vectors `reactive_output()` passes the R value through unchanged, and Shiny serializes it with `auto_unbox`, so a character vector of length one arrives as a string, not an array. In `app.R`, `output$files` sends the file names and the TidyTuesday date for the selected title, and `ui.js` joins the names into a single line with `files.names.join(", ")`. The spike's default title was Netflix Titles, which has one file. The app crashed on load, and the browser console showed: ```{.default} TypeError: files.names.join is not a function at App (http://127.0.0.1:8765/spike-1795455972/ui.js:16:61) at vf (http://127.0.0.1:8765/shinyreact-0.1.1/shinyreact.js:40:47833) at Yf (http://127.0.0.1:8765/shinyreact-0.1.1/shinyreact.js:40:70472) at Gd (http://127.0.0.1:8765/shinyreact-0.1.1/shinyreact.js:40:80765) at ry (http://127.0.0.1:8765/shinyreact-0.1.1/shinyreact.js:40:116187) at Kr (http://127.0.0.1:8765/shinyreact-0.1.1/shinyreact.js:40:115267) at uc (http://127.0.0.1:8765/shinyreact-0.1.1/shinyreact.js:40:115104) at cy (http://127.0.0.1:8765/shinyreact-0.1.1/shinyreact.js:40:111963) at My (http://127.0.0.1:8765/shinyreact-0.1.1/shinyreact.js:40:123483) at It (http://127.0.0.1:8765/shinyreact-0.1.1/shinyreact.js:17:1579) ``` Shiny's internal `toJSON()` shows why. One file arrives as a string, and two files arrive as an array: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="false"} # one file (Netflix Titles) shiny:::toJSON(list(names = c("netflix_titles.csv"))) #> {"names":"netflix_titles.csv"} ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="false"} # two files (Space Launches) shiny:::toJSON(list(names = c("agencies.csv", "launches.csv"))) #> {"names":["agencies.csv","launches.csv"]} ``` ::: #### The fix The spike fixed the client line with `[].concat()`, which turns a string into a one element array and leaves an array alone: ```{.default} files && h("p", { id: "files" }, "Files: ", [].concat(files.names).join(", "), " | TidyTuesday date: ", files.date), ``` We can also protect the vector on the server with `I()`, which keeps it an array: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="false"} shiny:::toJSON(list(names = I("netflix_titles.csv"))) #> {"names":["netflix_titles.csv"]} ``` ::: Or we can wrap it on the client, so every `reactive_output()` is covered. In the package, I went with a small client helper: ```{.default} export function asArray(x: T | T[] | null | undefined): T[] { if (x === null || x === undefined) return []; #<1> return Array.isArray(x) ? x : [x]; #<2> } ``` 1. Returns an empty array when there's no value yet (the output hasn't arrived, or the server sent `NULL`) 2. An array comes back unchanged, and a single value is wrapped in an array ## The conversion The conversion lives on its own branch, so `main` keeps the `bslib` app. The spike was built outside the repo, so the branch starts with the full conversion in one commit (`convert UI to shinyreact`). The graph below shows how the two branches diverge: ```{mermaid} %%| fig-width: 6 %%| fig-align: 'center' %%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'gitGraph': {'mainBranchName': 'main', 'showCommitLabel': true, 'rotateCommitLabel': true}, 'themeVariables': { 'fontFamily': 'monospace', "darkMode":false, 'git0': '#4CBB9D', 'git1': '#E83E8C', 'gitBranchLabel0': '#FFFFFF', 'gitBranchLabel1': '#FFFFFF', 'commitLabelFontSize': '12px'}}}%% gitGraph LR: commit id: "d3f3d7b" commit id: "ab7a2e3" commit id: "7202318" branch shinyreact checkout shinyreact commit id: "convert UI to shinyreact" type: HIGHLIGHT commit id: "796b3b7" checkout main commit id: "c03fa33" checkout shinyreact commit id: "5f4a1df" checkout main commit id: "0d16311" checkout shinyreact commit id: "0b6c43b" checkout main commit id: "f48c616" checkout shinyreact commit id: "92b21f4" ``` The branches don't share UI code anymore, so every change happens twice. I've added a few improvements to both (reordering the tabs, clearer graph labels, and the option to download one file or all files). I haven't decided whether to merge the two branches, so for now I've updated the documentation on each branch to describe its changes. ### The client The client is a Vite and TypeScript (TSX) project in `js/`. `npm run build` writes `inst/www/ui.js` and `ui.css`: ::: {style="font-style: italic;"} ```{.default} js/ ├── package-lock.json ├── package.json ├── src │ ├── components │ │ ├── DatasetSelect.tsx │ │ ├── Download.tsx │ │ ├── GraphsTab.tsx │ │ ├── ListTab.tsx │ │ ├── SummaryTab.tsx │ │ └── TitleInput.tsx │ ├── shinyreact.ts │ ├── ui.css │ └── ui.tsx ├── tsconfig.json └── vite.config.ts ``` ::: React isn't bundled, because `shinyreact.js` (served by the R package) already provides it, so Vite maps `react` to the global `shinyreact.React`: ```{.default} rollupOptions: { external: ["react"], #<1> output: { globals: { react: "shinyreact.React" } }, #<2> }, ``` 1. Leave React out of the bundle 2. At runtime, every `import ... from "react"` uses the copy that `shinyreact.js` provides `js/` is in `.Rbuildignore`, and the built bundle is committed, so installing the package doesn't require Node. The path from source files to the browser looks like this: ```{mermaid} %%| fig-width: 6 %%| fig-align: 'center' %%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'themeVariables': { 'fontFamily': 'monospace', "darkMode":false}}}%% flowchart TD Src[("js/src/
TSX components")] Build[["npm run build
(Vite)"]] WWW[("inst/www/
ui.js + ui.css")] UI[["app_ui()
page_react()"]] Br(["Browser"]) Src -->|"i. compile"| Build Build -->|"ii. write bundle"| WWW WWW -->|"iii. installed with
the package"| UI UI -->|"iv. serve"| Br style Src fill:#FFFFFF,color:#000000,stroke:#333 style Build fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF style WWW fill:#FFFFFF,color:#000000,stroke:#333 style UI fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF style Br fill:#FFFFFF,color:#000000,stroke:#333 ``` ### What happened to the modules? All the module UI functions are gone. The server module functions keep their `id`s, and the client wraps the matching component in a `ShinyModuleProvider` with the same namespace: ```{.default} #<1> ``` 1. Hook ids inside the provider get the `"input"` namespace, so `"ds_title"` becomes `input-ds_title` (the same id `NS("input")` creates for `mod_input_server("input")`) The namespace strings on the client have to match the module ids in `app_server()`: ```{mermaid} %%| fig-width: 6 %%| fig-align: 'center' %%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'themeVariables': { 'fontFamily': 'monospace', "darkMode":false}}}%% flowchart LR subgraph Cli["ui.tsx"] CI("TitleInput") CD("Download") CL("ListTab") CS("SummaryTab") CP("GraphsTab") end subgraph Srv["app_server()"] MI[["mod_input_server('input')"]] MD[["mod_download_server('download')"]] ML[["mod_list_server('listviewerlite')"]] MS[["mod_summary_server('summary')"]] MP[["mod_plot_server('viz')"]] end CI <-.->|"input"| MI CD <-.->|"download"| MD CL <-.->|"listviewerlite"| ML CS <-.->|"summary"| MS CP <-.->|"viz"| MP style Srv fill:#FFFFFF,color:#000000,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px,rx:10,ry:10 style Cli fill:#FFFFFF,color:#000000,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px,rx:10,ry:10 style MI fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF style MD fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF style ML fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF style MS fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF style MP fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF style CI fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF,rx:5,ry:5 style CD fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF,rx:5,ry:5 style CL fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF,rx:5,ry:5 style CS fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF,rx:5,ry:5 style CP fill:#4CBB9D,color:#FFFFFF,rx:5,ry:5 ``` ### Plain values Plain values (the dataset titles, file names, and the Summary file overview) moved to `reactive_output()`. For example, `mod_input_server()` used to get its choices from `selectInput()` in the UI module. Now it sends them: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="false"} output$titles <- shinyreact::reactive_output( unique(all_tt_combined$title[!is.na(all_tt_combined$data_files)]) ) ``` ::: And `TitleInput.tsx` reads the titles and sends the selection back as `input$ds_title`: ```{.default} const titles = asArray(useShinyOutputValue("titles", [])); const [title, setTitle] = useShinyInput("ds_title", "Space Launches"); #<1> ``` 1. `setTitle()` sends the selected title back as `input$ds_title` The table below maps each module to its outputs and client component: | Module | R output | Client | |---|---|---| | `mod_input` | `titles` (`reactive_output()`) | `TitleInput.tsx` | | `mod_download` | `files` (`reactive_output()`); `download` (`downloadHandler()`) | `Download.tsx` | | `mod_list` | `list` (`renderUI()`) | `ListTab.tsx` | | `mod_summary` | `overview`, `choices` (`reactive_output()`); `stats`, `vars`, `table` (`renderReactable()`) | `SummaryTab.tsx` | | `mod_plot` | `datasets` (`reactive_output()`); `plt_` (`renderPlot()`) | `GraphsTab.tsx` | ### What happened to the inputs? The inputs went the same way as the module UI functions. There's no `selectInput()` or `checkboxGroupInput()` left on the `shinyreact` branch. Each input is now React state that `useShinyInput()` copies to the server. The ids didn't change, so every `input$...` in the server modules reads the same value it did before. ```{.default} export function TitleInput() { const titles = asArray(useShinyOutputValue("titles", [])); #<1> const [title, setTitle] = useShinyInput("ds_title", "Space Launches"); #<2> return (
); } ``` 1. Dataset titles from `output$titles` (a `reactive_output()`), wrapped in `asArray()` in case only one title arrives 2. `title` holds the current value (`"Space Launches"` until the user picks one), and `setTitle()` sends it to the server as `input$ds_title` 3. The `` in `TitleInput.tsx` | | `mod_download` | `file` | `selectInput()` and `updateSelectInput()` | `` in `Download.tsx` | | `mod_summary` | `ds_input` | `selectInput()` and `updateSelectInput()` | `DatasetSelect.tsx` | | `mod_plot` | `dataset` | `selectInput()` and `updateSelectInput()` | `DatasetSelect.tsx` | | `mod_plot` | `plots` | `checkboxGroupInput()` | checkboxes in `GraphsTab.tsx` | #### Choices and selections `updateSelectInput()` is gone too. On `main`, the server changed a select's choices when a new title loaded. On `shinyreact`, the server only sends the choices (as a `reactive_output()`), and the client picks the selected value. `DatasetSelect.tsx` selects the first file whenever the file names change: ```{.default} const choices = asArray(useShinyOutputValue(props.outputId, null)); const [value, setValue] = useShinyInput(props.inputId, null); #<1> const key = choices.join("\u0000"); #<2> React.useEffect(() => { #<3> if (choices.length > 0 && (value === null || !choices.includes(value))) { setValue(choices[0]); } }, [key]); #<3> ``` 1. The selected file, sent as `input$dataset` (Graphs tab) or `input$ds_input` (Summary tab); the choices on the line above come from `output$datasets` or `output$choices` 2. One string built from all the file names, so the effect below runs only when the names change 3. Runs when a new title brings new file names. If the current file isn't among them, it selects the first one (this replaces `updateSelectInput()`) `Download.tsx` does the same thing for the file choice, but it resets to `"all"` instead of the first file. So the server decides what the choices are, and the client decides which one is selected. ### Plot outputs The plot module changed the most. The `bslib` version populated a dataset `selectInput()` with `updateSelectInput()`, created `renderPlot()` calls inside an observer, and built the plot containers with `renderUI()`. It also piped `return(...)` into `bindEvent()`, so the `bindEvent()` never ran. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="false"} # mod_plot_server() from main branch observe({ #<1> if (is.null(ttd_r())) { updateSelectInput(session, "dataset", choices = character(0)) return() } ds <- names(ttd_r()) updateSelectInput(session, "dataset", choices = ds, selected = ds[[1]]) }) |> bindEvent(ttd_r(), ignoreNULL = FALSE) #<1> observe({ #<2> ds_list <- req(ttd_r()) sel_ds <- input$dataset req(sel_ds %in% names(ds_list)) df <- ds_list[[sel_ds]] purrr::walk(input$plots, function(plt) { output[[paste0("plt_", plt)]] <- renderPlot({ inspect_plot(ttd = setNames(list(df), sel_ds), plots = plt) }) }) }) |> bindEvent(list(ttd_r(), input$dataset, input$plots), ignoreNULL = TRUE) #<2> output$plots_ui <- renderUI({ #<3> req(ttd_r(), input$dataset, input$plots) purrr::map(input$plots, function(plt) { tagList( h4(names(plot_labels())[plot_labels() == plt]), plotOutput(ns(paste0("plt_", plt)), height = "300px") ) }) }) #<3> return( #<4> reactive({ list("dataset" = input$dataset, "plots" = input$plots) }) ) |> bindEvent(list(ttd_r(), input$dataset, input$plots), ignoreNULL = TRUE) #<4> ``` ::: 1. Populate the dataset dropdown once ttd is available 2. Render each selected plot type for chosen dataset 3. Dynamically generate UI for selected plot types 4. `return()` exits before `bindEvent()` runs The new version creates one `renderPlot()` per plot type up front, and each one is gated by `req()`: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="false"} purrr::walk(PLOT_TYPES, function(plt) { output[[paste0("plt_", plt)]] <- renderPlot({ req(plt %in% input$plots) ds <- selected() #<1> tryCatch( inspect_plot(ttd = ds, plots = plt), error = function(err) { plot.new() text(0.5, 0.5, "Error generating plot", cex = 1.2, col = "red") } ) }) }) ``` ::: 1. outside `tryCatch()` so `req()` is not caught as an error The checkboxes and plot containers now live in `GraphsTab.tsx`, and `PLOT_TYPES` has to match in both places. ## Surprises in the conversion The conversion turned up two more surprises. ### Outputs that never rendered `app_server()` has a `dev` output (a `listview()` of the reactive values) in a closed `
